add_user_to_group.description: Put a user in a group, so they pick up whatever roles and attributes it carries. Adding someone who is already a member changes nothing and is not an error.
add_user_to_group.display_str_template: Add a Keycloak user to a group.
add_user_to_group.name: add_user_to_group

parameters.description: The user's Keycloak ID - the UUID in the admin console's address bar when the user is open, and the 'id' field of any List users result. Not the username, which can change.
parameters.name: user_id

parameters.description: The group to act on. Pick one, or paste a group ID from an earlier step - a group created by this workflow will not be in the list until it is refreshed.
parameters.name: group_id

assign_realm_role_to_user.description: Give a user a realm role. The role takes effect on their next token, so an already signed-in user picks it up when their session refreshes rather than instantly. Assigning a role the user already has changes nothing and is not an error.
assign_realm_role_to_user.display_str_template: Assign a Keycloak realm role to a user.
assign_realm_role_to_user.name: assign_realm_role_to_user

parameters.description: The user's Keycloak ID - the UUID in the admin console's address bar when the user is open, and the 'id' field of any List users result. Not the username, which can change.
parameters.name: user_id

parameters.description: The realm role, by name. Pick one, or type a name - a role created by this workflow will not be in the list until it is refreshed.
parameters.name: role_name

create_group.description: Create a top-level group and return it, including the new group ID for later steps. Group names are unique among their siblings.
create_group.name: create_group

parameters.description: The group's name.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: What the group is for.
parameters.name: description

create_realm_role.description: Create a realm role and return it. Role names are unique in the realm and are how every other role step refers to them, so pick a name you can keep.
create_realm_role.name: create_realm_role

parameters.description: The role's name, unique in the realm. This is the identifier applications check for.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: What the role grants.
parameters.name: description

create_user.description: Create a user in the realm and return the created record, including the new user ID for later steps. The username must be unique in the realm, and so is the email address when the realm requires one. Set a password here to create the account ready to use; leave it empty to create one that cannot sign in until a password is set.
create_user.name: create_user

parameters.description: The username, unique within the realm. Keycloak lowercases it unless the realm is set to be case sensitive.
parameters.name: username

parameters.description: The user's email address.
parameters.name: email

parameters.description: The user's first name.
parameters.name: first_name

parameters.description: The user's last name.
parameters.name: last_name

parameters.description: Whether the account can sign in. Defaults to enabled.
parameters.name: enabled

parameters.description: Mark the email as already verified, so the user is not asked to confirm it. Defaults to unverified.
parameters.name: email_verified

parameters.description: What the user must do at their next sign-in. Each one has to be switched on for the realm under Authentication > Required actions; Keycloak accepts one that is off and then simply never asks for it.
parameters.name: required_actions

parameters.description: An initial password. Leave empty to create the account without one.
parameters.name: password

parameters.description: Make the user choose a new password at their first sign-in. Defaults to a permanent password.
parameters.name: temporary_password

delete_group.description: Delete a group and its subgroups. The members keep their accounts and lose whatever the group granted them. This cannot be undone.
delete_group.name: delete_group

parameters.description: The group to act on. Pick one, or paste a group ID from an earlier step - a group created by this workflow will not be in the list until it is refreshed.
parameters.name: group_id

delete_realm_role.description: Delete a realm role by name. Everyone who held it loses it immediately, and any composite role built on it loses that part. This cannot be undone.
delete_realm_role.name: delete_realm_role

parameters.description: The realm role, by name. Pick one, or type a name - a role created by this workflow will not be in the list until it is refreshed.
parameters.name: role_name

delete_user.description: Permanently delete a user, with their sessions, group memberships and role assignments. This cannot be undone - to block someone's access reversibly, use Update user to disable the account instead.
delete_user.name: delete_user

parameters.description: The user's Keycloak ID - the UUID in the admin console's address bar when the user is open, and the 'id' field of any List users result. Not the username, which can change.
parameters.name: user_id

get_group.description: Read one group: its name, description, full path, parent and attributes.
get_group.name: get_group

parameters.description: The group to act on. Pick one, or paste a group ID from an earlier step - a group created by this workflow will not be in the list until it is refreshed.
parameters.name: group_id

get_user.description: Read one user in full by their Keycloak user ID: username, name, email and whether it is verified, whether the account is enabled, when it was created, and any required actions outstanding.
get_user.name: get_user

parameters.description: The user's Keycloak ID - the UUID in the admin console's address bar when the user is open, and the 'id' field of any List users result. Not the username, which can change.
parameters.name: user_id

list_clients.description: The applications registered in the realm, with each one's UUID, client ID, protocol, redirect URIs and which flows it allows. Search by part of a client ID, or turn off partial matching to look one up exactly.
list_clients.name: list_clients

parameters.description: Only clients whose client ID matches. Leave empty for all of them.
parameters.name: client_id

parameters.description: Treat the client ID above as text to search for rather than an exact name. Defaults to on, and does nothing unless a client ID is given.
parameters.display_name: Match part of the client ID
parameters.name: partial_match

parameters.description: Hide clients the service account has no view permission for, instead of listing them by ID alone.
parameters.name: viewable_only

parameters.description: How many results to skip before this page. Leave empty to start at the beginning.
parameters.name: offset

parameters.description: How many to return, 1-500. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

next_offset.description: The offset to send for the next page, if any

list_group_members.description: The users in a group. Members of its subgroups are not included - Keycloak treats each group's membership as its own.
list_group_members.display_str_template: List members of a Keycloak group.
list_group_members.name: list_group_members

parameters.description: The group to act on. Pick one, or paste a group ID from an earlier step - a group created by this workflow will not be in the list until it is refreshed.
parameters.name: group_id

parameters.description: How many results to skip before this page. Leave empty to start at the beginning.
parameters.name: offset

parameters.description: How many to return, 1-500. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

next_offset.description: The offset to send for the next page, if any

list_groups.description: The realm's top-level groups, each with its path and how many subgroups it has. Search by name to find one anywhere in the tree.
list_groups.name: list_groups

parameters.description: Only groups whose name matches this text. Leave empty for all of them.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description: Match the search text exactly instead of as part of a name.
parameters.name: exact

parameters.description: How many results to skip before this page. Leave empty to start at the beginning.
parameters.name: offset

parameters.description: How many to return, 1-500. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

next_offset.description: The offset to send for the next page, if any

list_realm_roles.description: The realm's own roles, with their descriptions and whether each is composite. Roles that belong to a client are listed under that client, not here.
list_realm_roles.name: list_realm_roles

parameters.description: Only roles whose name or description matches this text. Leave empty for all of them.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description: How many results to skip before this page. Leave empty to start at the beginning.
parameters.name: offset

parameters.description: How many to return, 1-500. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

next_offset.description: The offset to send for the next page, if any

list_user_realm_roles.description: The realm roles assigned directly to a user. Roles they hold only through a group, or through a composite role, are not listed here - Keycloak counts those as effective roles rather than as this user's own.
list_user_realm_roles.display_str_template: List a Keycloak user's realm roles.
list_user_realm_roles.name: list_user_realm_roles

parameters.description: The user's Keycloak ID - the UUID in the admin console's address bar when the user is open, and the 'id' field of any List users result. Not the username, which can change.
parameters.name: user_id

items.description: The realm roles assigned directly to the user

list_user_sessions.description: The user's active sessions: when each started, when it was last used, the IP address it came from and which applications it has reached. An empty list means the user is not signed in anywhere.
list_user_sessions.name: list_user_sessions

parameters.description: The user's Keycloak ID - the UUID in the admin console's address bar when the user is open, and the 'id' field of any List users result. Not the username, which can change.
parameters.name: user_id

list_users.description: Find users in the realm. Search across username, first name, last name and email at once, or filter on any of them individually, and narrow to enabled or verified accounts. Returns each user's ID, username, name, email and status.
list_users.name: list_users

parameters.description: Match this text against username, first name, last name and email at once. Leave empty for all users.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description: Only users with this username.
parameters.name: username

parameters.description: Only users with this email address.
parameters.name: email

parameters.description: Only users with this first name.
parameters.name: first_name

parameters.description: Only users with this last name.
parameters.name: last_name

parameters.description: Only enabled users, or only disabled ones. Leave unset for both.
parameters.name: enabled

parameters.description: Only users whose email is verified, or only those whose is not. Leave unset for both.
parameters.name: email_verified

parameters.description: Match the username, email and name filters exactly instead of as a prefix.
parameters.name: exact

parameters.description: How many results to skip before this page. Leave empty to start at the beginning.
parameters.name: offset

parameters.description: How many to return, 1-500. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: limit

next_offset.description: The offset to send for the next page, if any

remove_user_from_group.description: Take a user out of a group. Their account and everything else about it are untouched; they simply lose what the group granted.
remove_user_from_group.display_str_template: Remove a Keycloak user from a group.
remove_user_from_group.name: remove_user_from_group

parameters.description: The user's Keycloak ID - the UUID in the admin console's address bar when the user is open, and the 'id' field of any List users result. Not the username, which can change.
parameters.name: user_id

parameters.description: The group to act on. Pick one, or paste a group ID from an earlier step - a group created by this workflow will not be in the list until it is refreshed.
parameters.name: group_id

reset_user_password.description: Set a user's password. By default the password is temporary, so Keycloak makes the user choose their own at the next sign-in - which is what an administrator setting a password usually wants. The password is never echoed back in the result.
reset_user_password.name: reset_user_password

parameters.description: The user's Keycloak ID - the UUID in the admin console's address bar when the user is open, and the 'id' field of any List users result. Not the username, which can change.
parameters.name: user_id

parameters.description: The new password.
parameters.name: password

parameters.description: Make the user choose a new password at their next sign-in. Defaults to on.
parameters.name: temporary

update_user.description: Change a user's details. Only the fields you fill in change - everything else is left exactly as it was. Use this to enable or disable an account, correct a name or email, or set what the user must do at their next sign-in.
update_user.name: update_user

parameters.description: The user's Keycloak ID - the UUID in the admin console's address bar when the user is open, and the 'id' field of any List users result. Not the username, which can change.
parameters.name: user_id

parameters.description: A new email address. Leave empty to keep it.
parameters.name: email

parameters.description: A new first name. Leave empty to keep it.
parameters.name: first_name

parameters.description: A new last name. Leave empty to keep it.
parameters.name: last_name

parameters.description: Enable or disable the account. Disabling it signs the user out and refuses new sign-ins without deleting anything. Leave unset to keep it as it is.
parameters.name: enabled

parameters.description: Mark the email verified or unverified. Leave unset to keep it as it is.
parameters.name: email_verified

parameters.description: What the user must do at their next sign-in. Each one has to be switched on for the realm under Authentication > Required actions; Keycloak accepts one that is off and then simply never asks for it.
parameters.name: required_actions

description: Administer a Keycloak realm. Create and update users, reset passwords, enable and disable accounts, manage groups and their members, create realm roles and assign them, check who is signed in, and list the applications registered in the realm.
